findings.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start index (start_offset = cursor.offset), which Django ORM querysets reject. Django raises AssertionError('Negative indices are not allowed') on queryset[negative:stop]; the comment 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is fabricated — any admin hitting this endpoint with a crafted negative-offset cursor gets a 500.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator calls self.build_queryset(cursor_value, cursor.is_prev), but it inherits from BasePaginator which defines no build_queryset method — that method is defined on subclasses like OffsetPaginator/DateTimePaginator. Any request through the optimized path raises AttributeError: 'OptimizedCursorPaginator' object has no attribute 'build_queryset', producing a 500 for superusers with ?optimized_pagination=true.

[BUG] get_result calls self._is_asc(for_prev) in get_item_key, but _is_asc is a DateTimePaginator mixin method, not defined on BasePaginator, so OptimizedCursorPaginator lacks it. The first prev/next cursor computation calls get_item_key and raises AttributeError: '_is_asc', crashing every paginated request through this paginator with a 500.

[BUG] The endpoint reads organization_context.member.has_global_access, but member can be None (e.g. superuser not a member of the org), so this raises AttributeError instead of evaluating False. A superuser who is not a member of the organization gets a 500 on GET /api/0/organizations/<slug>/audit-logs/ even without the optimized flag, because the access check runs unconditionally.

[BUG] The endpoint passes enable_advanced_features=True into self.paginate(...), but the API paginate()/ApiPaginator plumbing forwards only fixed kwargs (paginator_cls, on_results, etc.) to the paginator constructor, so this kwarg raises TypeError. Any admin request with optimized_pagination=true fails with TypeError: unexpected keyword argument 'enable_advanced_features' (or the kwarg is silently dropped and the advanced branch never activates), depending on paginate's signature — either way the promised feature cannot work as written.

[ADVISORY] The DateTimePaginator get_result change alters slicing for is_prev cursors to pass through raw (possibly negative) offsets instead of clamping at 0. A malformed/adversarial prev cursor with a negative offset now reaches queryset slicing directly in the default non-optimized path, hitting the same Django negative-index AssertionError that the OptimizedCursorPaginator hits — a client-controlled 500 on the existing endpoint.

[BUG] The 'advanced' negative-offset slicing path passes a negative start_offset to a Django QuerySet slice, which Django rejects. Django's QuerySet slicing raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported') for any slice with a negative start, so any admin request with optimized_pagination=true and a cursor carrying a negative offset returns a 500 error instead of paginated results — the feature crashes on its own advertised happy path.

[BUG] The gate `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` references `organization_context`, a name that is never defined in this view's scope. Every GET to the organization audit logs endpoint that sets optimized_pagination=true raises NameError on organization_context, returning a 500 to all clients (admin or not) instead of the paginated audit rows.

[BUG] The prev-cursor boundary check compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the raw (possibly negative) cursor offset rather than the clamped start_offset actually used for slicing. For any prev-cursor whose offset is negative, the equality check uses a different index basis than the slice that produced `results`, so the duplicate-boundary row is never trimmed and clients receive the row already seen on the previous page (or the last row is silently dropped), producing duplicated/missing audit entries across pages.

[BUG] The modified base get_result clamps negative offsets to 0 only when `not cursor.is_prev`, silently changing slice bounds for negative-offset forward cursors that previously raised. A forward cursor with offset=-5 that previously failed fast now silently reads from index 0, returning rows the client already paginated past; any API consumer relying on the old error to detect a corrupted/forged cursor now gets silently wrong data instead.

[ADVISORY] The new optimized pagination path is gated on a raw query parameter (optimized_pagination=true) with no feature flag, options entry, or documented API surface, and the diff adds zero tests for either the endpoint branch or the new OptimizedCursorPaginator. Operators cannot disable the crashing negative-offset path without a code deploy, and the entire new paginator class (get_item_key rounding, negative-offset slicing, prev-cursor trimming) ships with no verification anywhere — a regression in audit-log pagination (a compliance-relevant data surface) would ship undetected; the diff contains no test-shaped files covering this behavior.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.dry-run claim of 'backward compatibility with existing cursor implementations' is unverified: its get_result is a near-duplicate of BasePaginator.get_result with drifted boundary logic (the max(0, offset) clamp duplicated from the diff above), creating two hand-maintained copies of the pagination algorithm. The next bug fix applied to one get_result copy (e.g., a prev-cursor off-by-one fix in the base class) will not propagate to the other, and admins toggling optimized_pagination will silently get different pagination semantics for the same cursor — the duplicate block is the concrete drift point already visible in this diff.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset path slices the queryset with a negative start, which Django ORM explicitly forbids. When an authorized admin passes a cursor with a negative offset and enable_advanced_features=True, `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` (Django QuerySet slicing), returning a 500 instead of results — the comment 'The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is false.

[BUG] The diff modifies BasePaginator.get_result's slicing logic for every existing paginator, which is scope drift beyond the audit-log pagination intent. All endpoints using this base path (groups, events, etc.) silently change slicing behavior: for prev cursors with offset < 0, `start_offset = offset` (unclamped) now passes a negative index to queryset slicing, raising the same Django negative-index AssertionError where the old code (`queryset[offset:stop]` — also negative but at least previously analyzed/unchanged) never changed behavior; this unrelated expansion alters pagination for the entire API surface to serve one endpoint's optimization.

[BUG] The prev-cursor dedup check compares `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` using the raw `offset`, not `start_offset`, so the negative-offset branch computed a different slice than the length check assumes. When offset is negative and the advanced path is taken, results were sliced from `start_offset = cursor.offset` with length limit+extra, but the equality check tests against `offset + limit + extra`, so the trailing duplicate row is never trimmed (or trimmed wrongly), returning duplicated rows to admin clients on prev pagination.

[ADVISORY] The new behavior is gated on a raw `optimized_pagination=true` query parameter with no feature flag, options entry, or documented API contract — implementation not traceable to any stated requirement. Operators cannot disable the new paginator without a code deploy, and the API silently exposes an undocumented parameter whose response shape (negative offsets, cursor semantics) differs from the documented one; out-of-tree clients discovering it get unsupported behavior.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near-verbatim copy of the existing DateTimePaginator/OffsetPaginator get_result body with three lines changed — duplicated logic block with no deletion of the original. The next bug fix to cursor pagination (e.g., the dedup logic above) must now be applied in two places and will drift; passing the deletion test fails because nothing becomes unnecessary — the ~90-line class duplicates logic that a keyword flag on the existing paginator already encodes (`enable_advanced_features`), which is exactly what the base-class change at line 179 already half-does, creating two parallel mechanisms for the same 'feature'.

[ADVISORY] The permission gate `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` grants the optimized path based on privilege level, but the paginator's only claimed difference is performance — no requirement ties performance features to admin authorization. Non-admin org owners get a silently different (slower, different cursor semantics) response for the identical request, and the 'advanced features' (negative offsets) are exactly the kind of thing that changes data exposure, so a future maintainer cannot tell whether the gate is a security boundary or an arbitrary privilege perk — the invariant the gate enforces is unstateable from the diff.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator (new non-trivial behavior: negative offset slicing, custom get_item_key with floor/ceil) ships with no tests anywhere in the diff. A regression in the floor/ceil key computation or the negative-offset path breaks admin audit-log pagination silently (duplicate/missing rows), and nothing in CI would catch it; the new `Cursor(0, 0, 0)` default and `cursor_value = 0` fallback also diverge from the existing paginators' behavior with no coverage.

[ADVISORY] The cursors.py change is a comment-only edit claiming negative offsets are supported, but no code change in that file enforces or validates it. The comment documents behavior that (per the Django slicing AssertionError above) actually crashes, so the next reader trusts a false invariant — stale/misleading doc-drift on a security-relevant value object.

[BUG] The 'advanced feature' negative-offset slicing produces wrong data: Django's queryset[-n:m] slices from the END of the ordered dataset, not from an arbitrary prior position. An admin passing a cursor with a negative offset gets rows counted backwards from the tail of the audit-log table (e.g. queryset[-100:-100+limit]) — a completely different page than requested, plus it forces the ORM into a compensating ORDER BY + subquery, defeating the claimed performance goal. The comment 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds' describes semantics the ORM does not have.

[BUG] get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on the key value, which is a datetime for this endpoint (order_by='-datetime'), raising TypeError. When used as the audit-log paginator with key='datetime', int(math.floor(datetime)) raises TypeError, so every optimized-path request returns a 500 instead of paginated rows. The code was copied from the integer-key OffsetPaginator family without adapting the value type, mirroring DateTimePaginator's datetime handling.

[BUG] The prev-page dedup branch compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra with an offset that can be negative, so the branch can never match (or matches spuriously), and slicing results[:-1] drops the wrong row. On a prev cursor with negative offset, offset+limit+extra is a negative length target that len(results) can never equal, so the boundary item is never stripped and duplicate rows appear at page boundaries for admin users.

[ADVISORY] Two hand-maintained parallel pagination code paths (optimized vs default) in the endpoint will drift, and the only difference is the paginator class plus an enable_advanced_features flag the paginator's own code paths share with BasePaginator. Any future fix to the shared slicing/boundary logic in BasePaginator.get_result (e.g. the negative-offset change already made there) must be replicated in OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, which already copies ~60 lines of it verbatim; the next maintainer of pagination correctness gets two copies to update and one silently misses fixes.

[BUG] The BasePaginator change alters slicing for prev cursors: previously stop = offset + limit + extra from a non-negative offset; now for cursor.is_prev the offset is used unclamped, so a prev cursor carrying a negative offset slices from the dataset end for ALL paginators, not just the optimized one. Any client that crafts a cursor with negative offset (Cursor.offset comes straight from the client-decoded cursor) hits queryset[-n:...] against every DateTimePaginator user in the entire codebase, returning rows from the table tail — a cross-cutting behavior change to shared pagination infrastructure gated by nothing.

[ADVISORY] The feature is gated on a raw query param 'optimized_pagination' plus an is_superuser/global-access check with no feature flag, and the paginator it selects provides no measurable performance benefit (same queryset, same slicing, same count path). Operators cannot disable or roll this path out gradually (no options entry/flag), and the code adds a privileged-only second path that returns 500s (datetime TypeError) whenever an admin opts in — the worst possible blast radius selection, since it puts the broken path behind the most privileged users.

[ADVISORY] value_from_cursor returns cursor.value directly and the None-cursor path builds Cursor(0,0,0), conflating the sentinel 0 with a real key value, and build_queryset(0, ...) filters on value 0 rather than 'no cursor'. A first page request with no cursor builds a queryset filtered against key value 0 (e.g. datetime <= 0 / id > 0 depending on the key), silently dropping rows whose key equals or precedes 0 or, for datetime keys, filtering on epoch-zero and returning an empty or wrong first page instead of the natural head of the dataset.

[ADVISORY] The offset field is documented as accepting negative values for 'advanced pagination' but nothing in the cursor (de)serialization or the main OffsetPaginator path defines what a negative offset means, leaving two paginators interpreting the same cursor bytes differently. A cursor produced by the optimized path (negative offset) handed back to the default DateTimePaginator endpoint variant (e.g. after an admin's flag is dropped, or a non-admin teammate opens the shared URL) is interpreted by different slicing rules, returning a different page for the same cursor — the cursor is no longer a stable contract across the endpoint's own two code paths.

[BUG] The enable_advanced_features branch slices the queryset with a negative start offset (start_offset = cursor.offset when cursor.offset < 0), which Django's QuerySet does not support. Any admin request to /organizations/<org>/auditlogs/ with optimized_pagination=true and a cursor carrying a negative offset raises ValueError/AssertionError ('Negative indexing is not supported') from the ORM, returning a 500 instead of paginated results — the advertised 'advanced pagination' path can never succeed.

[BUG] The prev-page dedup check compares len(results) == offset + limit + extra using the raw (possibly negative) cursor.offset rather than the clamped start_offset, so the boundary-trim branch never fires for negative offsets. When is_prev with a negative offset doesn't crash first, the duplicate cursor-value row that the trim is supposed to remove is returned to the client, producing duplicated audit-log rows across page transitions.

[BUG] The BasePaginator.get_result change now passes a negative offset through unclamped whenever cursor.is_prev is true (`max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`), changing behavior for every existing DateTimePaginator/OffsetPaginator caller on the prev path. Every endpoint that paginates backwards with a cursor whose offset goes negative (previously clamped to 0) now hits Django's negative-slice ValueError and 500s — a regression in the shared base class affecting far more than audit logs, with no human acceptance of this base-class contract change.

[ADVISORY] New pagination behavior is gated on a raw query parameter (optimized_pagination=true) plus an ad-hoc permission expression (is_superuser or member.has_global_access) with no feature flag, options entry, or documented API contract change. The same endpoint silently returns two different cursor/pagination semantics (DateTimePaginator cursors vs OptimizedCursorPaginator cursors) depending on an undocumented query param, so API consumers who copy/paste cursors between clients or sessions get unpredictable result sets, and operators cannot disable the path without a code deploy; the security/permission gate was also never part of the stated PR objective (pagination performance).

[ADVISORY] organization_context.member.has_global_access is evaluated without a None guard on organization_context, diverging from how access checks are performed elsewhere in this endpoint. Superusers on control-silo requests where organization_context is None get an AttributeError and a 500 instead of the optimized pagination the code intends to grant them.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result constructs a default cursor as Cursor(0, 0, 0), discarding the caller's actual default-cursor semantics used by other paginators. Maintainers extending BasePaginator now have two divergent default-cursor constructions to keep in sync; a change to default cursor construction in BasePaginator will silently not apply to this subclass, breaking next/prev link generation for the optimized path.

[BUG] The BasePaginator.get_result change allows a negative offset whenever cursor.is_prev is true, and cursor.offset is decoded from the client-supplied cursor string, so any client can drive queryset slicing with a negative index. Django's QuerySet slicing raises ValueError('Negative indices are not allowed') for any negative start, so a crafted ?cursor= value with a negative offset on any endpoint using this paginator turns the request into an unhandled 500 — a remotely triggerable availability/DoS failure across all DateTimePaginator-style endpoints, not just the audit log one.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result's enable_advanced_features branch executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a start_offset taken directly from the client-controlled cursor offset, and Django's ORM rejects negative slice indices rather than 'handling boundary conditions automatically' as the comment claims. A superuser or global-access member sending a cursor whose decoded offset is negative gets a ValueError from the ORM, an unhandled 500 on the audit-log endpoint, and a corrupted response — the comment's safety claim ('the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing') is factually false, so the whole 'advanced negative offset' feature crashes on first use with any negative offset.

[ADVISORY] The new pagination behavior is gated on a raw query parameter (optimized_pagination=true) plus an in-code is_superuser/has_global_access check, with no feature flag or options entry, and the security justification lives only in comments ('this is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') rather than in any enforced boundary. Operators cannot disable the new paginator path without a code deploy if it misbehaves, and the comment-based trust claim hides that the paginator additionally trusts the client-supplied cursor offset verbatim (see the negative-offset findings); the next reader assumes a validated offset boundary that does not exist and builds on it.

[BUG] The advanced-feature path slices the queryset with a negative start offset, which Django's ORM raises ValueError/AssertionError for ('Negative indexing is not supported' on QuerySet slicing), so the request 500s instead of returning a page. Any client that obtains a cursor with a negative offset and hits the OptimizedCursorPaginator path with enable_advanced_features=True gets a 500 on every subsequent page request; the promised 'efficient reverse pagination' never works at all.

[BUG] enable_advanced evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally, crashing with AttributeError when member is None (superusers or non-member admins have no organization membership). Superusers and staff without membership in the requested organization receive a 500 instead of the audit log listing; also the boolean check itself is evaluated even when use_optimized is false, so the crash triggers on every request for those users.

[ADVISORY] The new OptimizedCursorPaginator behavior is gated on a raw query param 'optimized_pagination' plus a runtime privilege check, with no options entry or feature flag, so it cannot be disabled or enabled for a subset of organizations without a code deploy. Operators responding to an incident caused by the new paginator path (e.g. the negative-offset 500s) have no kill switch; they must roll back the deploy, extending the outage window for a high-traffic endpoint.

[ADVISORY] The base-paginator change alters the non-prev branch from `stop = offset + limit + extra` to clamping start_offset with max(0, offset) while computing stop from start_offset, changing slice semantics for negative offsets on the shared DateTimePaginator path for all endpoints. Every existing endpoint using OffsetPaginator-derived get_result now silently produces different (empty) result sets for crafted negative-offset cursors instead of raising, a behavior change on shared infrastructure made for a feature only used by the audit-log endpoint.

[ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result duplicates ~60 lines of BasePaginator/OffsetPaginator.get_result with only the negative-offset branch differing, so future fixes to the shared pagination logic (cursor building, boundary trimming) will need to be applied twice and will drift. The next pagination bugfix applied only to the base class leaves the optimized path broken; deletion of the duplicated method (subclassing with only the slicing override) removes ~55 lines.

[BUG] The prev-cursor path passes a negative offset straight into Django queryset slicing, which raises an exception and returns a 500 where the cursor contract expects a valid page. A client supplying a crafted prev cursor with a negative offset (cursor.offset is attacker-controlled via the base64 cursor) hits `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with start_offset < 0; Django ORM raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), the audit-logs endpoint 500s instead of returning a 4xx/empty page, and the user sees an error for a request the paginator previously handled by clamping.

[BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator's 'advanced negative offset' branch slices the queryset with a negative start, which Django's ORM rejects, so every request using that feature crashes. When `enable_advanced_features=True` and cursor.offset < 0, `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raises ValueError from the Django ORM (negative slicing is unsupported), producing a raw 500 on the organization audit-logs endpoint. The comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' — that is factually wrong, so the entire advertised feature can never serve a successful response and fails as an unhandled 500.

[BUG] The prev-page duplicate-removal check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares against the pre-clamp offset, so with a negative (or clamped) offset the branch never fires and the boundary row is returned twice. When cursor.value matches no first-row key (e.g. ties in the datetime key) and offset was clamped to 0 while the comparison still uses the raw negative offset, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` is never true, `results[:-1]` is not applied, and the client receives the cursor-boundary row duplicated on consecutive prev pages — silent data desync in pagination output reported as success.

[BUG] `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is accessed without a None check, so a superuser who is not a member of the organization crashes the endpoint before pagination. A superuser (or any user reaching this code where the org member record is absent, e.g. admin views of orgs they don't belong to) gets AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'has_global_access', returning a raw 500 on a GET that previously succeeded via the DateTimePaginator path — even for requests that never asked for optimized pagination, since the flag is evaluated unconditionally on every request.

[ADVISORY] The new pagination behavior is gated on a raw query parameter `optimized_pagination=true` with no feature flag or options entry, so it cannot be disabled short of a code deploy. Operators hitting a regression in OptimizedCursorPaginator (e.g. the negative-offset 500 above) have no kill switch: every audit-log request that includes the param from a saved link or client build keeps triggering the broken code path until a rollback deploy, and there is no way to audit which clients are using it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The DateTimePaginator get_result change alters slicing for is_prev cursors to pass through raw (possibly negative) offsets instead of clamping at 0. A malformed/adversarial prev cursor with a negative offset now reaches queryset slicing directly in the default non-optimized path, hitting the same Django negative-index AssertionError that the OptimizedCursorPaginator hits — a client-controlled 500 on the existing endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The cited change in `paginator.py` does not newly “pass through raw (possibly negative) offsets” for `is_prev` cursors. Before the diff, slicing already used `queryset[offset:stop]` (raw `offset` for both prev and non-prev). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result constructs a default cursor as Cursor(0, 0, 0), discarding the caller's actual default-cursor semantics used by other paginators. However, the diff alone does not prove that other paginators use different defaults or that next/prev links are currently broken, so it’s not a verifiable correctness bug from the diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The BasePaginator.get_result change allows a negative offset whenever cursor.is_prev is true, and cursor.offset is decoded from the client-supplied cursor string, so any client can drive queryset slicing with a negative index. Django's QuerySet slicing raises ValueError('Negative indices are not allowed') for any negative start, so a crafted ?cursor= value with a negative offset on any endpoint using this paginator turns the request into an unhandled 500 — a remotely triggerable availability/DoS failure across all DateTimePaginator-style endpoints, not just the audit log one.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/api/paginator.py` the updated `BasePaginator.get_result` computes `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset`, so when `cursor.is_prev` is true it will pass a potentially negative `offset` directly into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. The diff also explicitly introduces/endorses negative offsets (comments and `OptimizedCursorPaginator` branch that sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` when `< 0`). Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative start indices and will raise (commonly `ValueError: Negative indices are not allowed`), which would surface as an unhandled 500 if a negative offset cursor is received.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result's enable_advanced_features branch executes list(queryset[start_offset:stop]) with a start_offset taken directly from the client-controlled cursor offset, and Django's ORM rejects negative slice indices rather than 'handling boundary conditions automatically' as the comment claims. A superuser or global-access member sending a cursor whose decoded offset is negative gets a ValueError from the ORM, an unhandled 500 on the audit-log endpoint, and a corrupted response — the comment's safety claim ('the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing') is factually false, so the whole 'advanced negative offset' feature crashes on first use with any negative offset.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and executes `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])`. The diff explicitly intends to allow negative slicing (“Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically”), but Django `QuerySet` slicing does not support negative indices and raises an exception, and this code does not catch it. Since the audit-log endpoint passes `enable_advanced_features=True` for authorized users (`paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` with `enable_advanced_features=True`), a client-provided cursor with a negative decoded offset would crash the request (500).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The advanced-feature path slices the queryset with a negative start offset, which Django's ORM raises ValueError/AssertionError for ('Negative indexing is not supported' on QuerySet slicing), so the request 500s instead of returning a page. Any client that obtains a cursor with a negative offset and hits the OptimizedCursorPaginator path with enable_advanced_features=True gets a 500 on every subsequent page request; the promised 'efficient reverse pagination' never works at all.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] enable_advanced evaluates organization_context.member.has_global_access unconditionally, crashing with AttributeError when member is None (superusers or non-member admins have no organization membership). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The base-paginator change alters the non-prev branch from `stop = offset + limit + extra` to clamping start_offset with max(0, offset) while computing stop from start_offset, changing slice semantics for negative offsets on the shared DateTimePaginator path for all endpoints. The finding’s specific claim that this will produce “empty” result sets isn’t supported by the new code (it would slice from 0 and likely return the first page), but the broader concern about an unscoped behavior change on shared infrastructure for negative offsets is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The prev-cursor path passes a negative offset straight into Django queryset slicing, which raises an exception and returns a 500 where the cursor contract expects a valid page. A client supplying a crafted prev cursor with a negative offset (cursor.offset is attacker-controlled via the base64 cursor) hits `list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` with start_offset < 0; Django ORM raises ValueError ('Negative indexing is not supported'), the audit-logs endpoint 500s instead of returning a 4xx/empty page, and the user sees an error for a request the paginator previously handled by clamping.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/expands paths that can pass a negative `cursor.offset` directly into Django queryset slicing. In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and does `queryset[start_offset:stop]`, which in Django ORM raises an exception for negative slice indices (negative indexing not supported). Additionally, the earlier paginator change keeps `start_offset = offset` when `cursor.is_prev`, so a negative `offset` on a prev cursor is still not clamped. Since cursor offsets come from the (client-controlled) cursor, this can trigger a 500 instead of returning an empty/handled page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] OptimizedCursorPaginator's 'advanced negative offset' branch slices the queryset with a negative start, which Django's ORM rejects, so every request using that feature crashes. When `enable_advanced_features=True` and cursor.offset < 0, `queryset[start_offset:stop]` raises ValueError from the Django ORM (negative slicing is unsupported), producing a raw 500 on the organization audit-logs endpoint. The comment claims 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' — that is factually wrong, so the entire advertised feature can never serve a successful response and fails as an unhandled 500.

adjudication.rationale: In `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result`, when `self.enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, it sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet slicing rejects negative start/stop values and raises `ValueError` (negative indexing/slicing is unsupported), so this branch will crash any request that hits it. The comment claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing is contradicted by Django’s documented behavior, making the advertised feature non-functional and causing a 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The prev-page duplicate-removal check `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` compares against the pre-clamp offset, so with a negative (or clamped) offset the branch never fires and the boundary row is returned twice. When cursor.value matches no first-row key (e.g. ties in the datetime key) and offset was clamped to 0 while the comparison still uses the raw negative offset, `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` is never true, `results[:-1]` is not applied, and the client receives the cursor-boundary row duplicated on consecutive prev pages — silent data desync in pagination output reported as success.

adjudication.rationale: The described mismatch depends on `offset` being clamped to 0 (via `start_offset = max(0, offset)`) while the duplicate-removal check still uses the raw negative `offset`. In the diff, that clamping only happens when `not cursor.is_prev`, but the duplicate-removal logic (`if cursor.is_prev and cursor.value: ... elif len(results) == offset + limit + extra: ...`) runs only when `cursor.is_prev` is true. In both the original paginator change and the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator`, when `cursor.is_prev` is true, `start_offset` is set to `offset` (no clamp), so the specific “clamped-to-0 but compared against negative” situation does not occur as claimed.
